g.text: The agent path ships first-class rather than as an afterthought:
AGENTS.md for any LLM, CLAUDE.md for `claude-code` auto-load, and
an installable claude-code skill. The agent isn't an "integration"
bolted on — it's one of your clients.
The mental model is deliberately single-user: one person, many
devices, many local agents, all bound by a tailnet (or LAN, or VPN).
No multi-user auth, no sharing mode, no ACLs. That one constraint
is what lets the whole thing stay tiny and feel instant — "open the
What you actually use it for: handing a file to an agent on another
machine, getting a URL or text blob back from it, parking a
screenshot or PDF so you can grab it from any device later. Same
shape every direction. Simple, fast, secure.
Implementation is ~1600 lines of Python stdlib (no `pip install`
for the server; HTML/CSS/JS is inlined). Text autosaves 400 ms
after your last keystroke; other clients pick up changes within ~2
s via X-Rev polling. Uploads show a progress bar that tracks the
can back up the entire state with `rsync`.
Things it deliberately doesn't do: multi-user auth, encryption at
rest, public-internet hosting, chat features, threads, presence.
penpad is a primitive, not a platform.
